description:
Surfaced 2026-05-08 by POLYBIUS during ariadne--m5e arc. Distillation of the SPEC-vs-shipped 'error: true' defect lesson from PR 1.SPEC (ariadne--hhb).

## Problem class

The m5e arc shipped PR 1 (server-side) with an internally-consistent design-rev3.md. Post-ship, when PR 1.SPEC was authored to align SPEC.md to the shipped wire shape, ADA copied JSON example fields verbatim from design-rev3.md §2.6 — including 'error: true' in three response examples. The shipped server actually strips the 'error' key before emit (routes.py:316), so the design's examples did NOT match shipped reality.

CATO caught it on review. ARGUS rev3 had not caught it because the design was internally consistent — only cross-referencing against shipped code reveals the gap. ARGUS is working as intended (its job is design-internal consistency + load-bearing risk, not diff-vs-shipped). The catch happened where it should — CATO. But the underlying drift is symptomatic of two missing disciplines:

## Two related items

### Item 1: ADA brief preamble grounding-check sharpening

Current MAJOR_PLINY.md ADA-brief shape includes generic 'ground against shipped code' instruction. The m5e ADA absorbed the design's defect anyway. Sharper version: enumerate explicit ground-check categories, not generic instruction.

Proposed enumeration:
- JSON example shapes (response bodies, request bodies)
- Function/method signatures (parameter names, types, return types)
- Error message text (exact string match)
- Line ranges in path:line citations
- HTTP response codes
- Wire-protocol constants (header names, status codes, envelope keys)

ADA brief preamble template gets a literal: 'Ground-check every concrete example in the design against the shipped code, specifically: [list above]. If a design example contradicts the shipped code, the shipped code is canon — flag the design drift but build to ship reality.'

This is a small substrate edit to MAJOR_PLINY.md's ADA-brief template/section.

### Item 2: Per-arc-closeout design-audit step

Current arc-closeout housekeeping has no 'audit design canon against shipped code' step. Today, design-rev3.md §2.6 still carries the 'error: true' defect; we caught it because PR 1.SPEC drove a re-read, not because of any routine audit. In a different arc shape (e.g., a single-PR arc), the defect could persist forever in the design canon.

Proposed close-out step: when an arc fully closes (all PRs shipped), one housekeeping task is 'walk through design canon (every design-rev*.md in agents/design/<ticket>/) and align to shipped code.' Specifically:
- Verify JSON examples match shipped wire shape
- Verify function signatures match shipped code
- Verify line ranges in citations are current
- Correct any drift in the design as small follow-up commits

This becomes a routine per-arc close-out task in MAJOR_PLINY.md alongside the existing close-out items (post-mortem, bw comment, etc.).

## Scope

- MAJOR_PLINY.md — ADA-brief preamble template (Item 1) + arc-closeout housekeeping checklist (Item 2)

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball. Pure substrate-doc edit; no code change.

## Out of scope

- ARGUS role expansion to cover design-vs-shipped drift — explicitly NOT recommended; would create role-collapse pressure with CATO. ARGUS stays as design-internal-consistency + load-bearing-risk.
- New pipeline stage between design and execute — adding ceremony for a problem already solved by sharper executor discipline + arc closeout audit.

## Empirical anchor

ariadne--m5e arc 2026-05-08:
- design-rev3.md §2.6 lines 171/191/206 contain 'error: true' in JSON response examples
- routes.py:316 strips 'error' key before raise
- tests/verification/ariadne--m5e/test_routes_confirmation.py:128 asserts body.get('error') is not True
- ADA on PR 1.SPEC (ariadne--hhb) absorbed the design's defect; CATO caught it; revision shipped clean as PR #30 / cb613b3
- design-rev3 §2.6 itself remains uncorrected pending m5e arc-close housekeeping batch (per the running brief)

## Bundle-shape rule (substrate observation, 2026-05-08)

CATO surfaced an empirical-substrate-rule observation during Engagement A (ariadne polish-batch, 2026-05-08 PRs #32/#33). The ariadne PLINY bundled three tickets (rv0, e9p, tjw.2) into one engagement; CATO reviewed the resulting diff cleanly with one minor hygiene finding. CATO explicitly named the meta-pattern after the review:

> 'narrow-server + client-polish + docs surfaces don't intersect, so bundle reviewed cleanly. Future routing input: bundle shape is safe when surfaces are disjoint.'

This is a real engagement-shape discipline that should land in MAJOR_PLINY.md alongside the per-arc-closeout audit step this ticket already covers.

### Proposed substrate addition

Add to MAJOR_PLINY.md (engagement-bundling section, alongside the closeout-audit content):

**Bundle-shape rule** — multiple tickets can ride in one engagement when their surfaces are *disjoint* (non-intersecting files / layers / concerns). Disjoint surfaces let CATO review cleanly because each sub-section of the diff is logically independent. Intersecting surfaces (multiple tickets editing the same file or coupled-by-control-flow code paths) should split into separate engagements; the gauntlet ceremony cost is justified by the review-clarity gain.

Empirical instances:
- Disjoint, bundle-safe: server-side max_length + SPEC.md docs + client-side polish (rv0 + e9p + tjw.2 → PRs #32/#33, 2026-05-08).
- Disjoint, bundle-safe: three separate SPEC.md sub-sections (opq + tjw.1 + 4d1 — three distinct doc additions in three different SPEC sub-trees, 2026-05-07 Batch H).
- Intersecting, split-required: m5e architectural pivots (multiple ticket revisions all touching the same design + same code paths; required separate gauntlets per revision).

PLINY's routing call when receiving a multi-ticket engagement scope from POLYBIUS:
1. Map each ticket's primary surface (file, function, or substrate area).
2. If all surfaces are disjoint → bundle is safe; one engagement, one CATO review.
3. If any surfaces overlap → split into separate engagements; surface to POLYBIUS if PR-shape decision needs ratification.

This rule is independent of the closeout audit step (which is about post-ship correctness verification) but lives alongside it as another MAJOR_PLINY.md substrate discipline.

Folded into this ticket's scope rather than filing a separate ticket because both items are MAJOR_PLINY.md edits and ride naturally in the same substrate-grooming dispatch.
